mechanism_narrative: The four-week downward drift in RETAIL_REC (-14.0 to -26.0) reflects an entrenched reduction in discretionary mobility that will persist by inertia, so the next four weekly means will continue at or below the current depressed level rather than rebound.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically from -14.0 to -26.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC exceeds the last 28-day mean by more than 2 points despite the prior monotonic decline, the inertia mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp week-on-week rise in RESIDENTIAL time above a 15-point threshold signals households shifting toward home-centered routines, which crowds out retail and recreation trips within the following week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL exceeds 15 points above baseline for the current week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 9.7 to 16.9 over the snapshot, crossing 15 in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises week-over-week immediately following a week where RESIDENTIAL exceeds 15, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp declines in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT indicate compounding policy-driven mobility restrictions (e.g., reduced commuting and transit curtailment), which jointly suppress retail footfall more than either series would alone, depressing RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both fall more than 15 points week-on-week in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell from -3.4 to -40.3 and TRANSIT fell from -10.0 to -27.7 between t-3w and t-1w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to decline further (or rebounds) despite concurrent drops exceeding 15 points in both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT, the interaction mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a winter-season regime, stable low PARKS mobility (around -19 to -21) indicates limited outdoor substitution for retail activity, meaning RETAIL_REC will continue to track indoor-constrained behavior and remain depressed over the next four weeks rather than recover via outdoor-linked retail traffic.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS remained between -19.3 and -21.1 across all four weeks with no seasonal uptick
regime_hint: winter season with limited outdoor substitution
failure_condition: If PARKS mobility rises sharply (more than 10 points) alongside a rebound in RETAIL_REC, indicating seasonal outdoor substitution effects, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated GROCERY_PHARM mobility relative to baseline reflects a substitution effect where essential shopping trips replace discretionary retail and recreation trips, so weeks with GROCERY_PHARM above 45 points will coincide with further RETAIL_REC declines within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM exceeds 45 points above baseline in the current week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached 48.0, 55.1, and 41.1 while RETAIL_REC fell concurrently
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM reading above 45, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The steep TRANSIT decline directly reduces the physical accessibility of retail and recreation destinations, so a one-week transit drop greater than 10 points will produce a corresponding RETAIL_REC decline within the next two weeks as commuters and shoppers lose transit-dependent access.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 10 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -15.1 to -27.7 between t-2w and t-1w, a drop of 12.6 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline within two weeks following a TRANSIT drop greater than 10 points, the accessibility mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in RESIDENTIAL combined with a sharp fall in WORKPLACES signals an active stay-at-home policy enforcement regime, where the compounded effect of both behavioral shifts suppresses RETAIL_REC more severely than either alone, with effects persisting over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises above 15 points while WORKPLACES falls below -20 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL reached 16.9 and WORKPLACES reached -21.6 in t-0w simultaneously
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL exceeding 15 and WORKPLACES below -20 concurrently, the compounded policy mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: The partial rebound of WORKPLACES from -40.3 to -21.6 in the most recent week signals an early reopening of commuting activity, which will translate into a modest recovery of RETAIL_REC within the following week as workplace-adjacent retail trips resume.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 15 points week-on-week after a prior decline
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -40.3 in t-1w to -21.6 in t-0w, an improvement of 18.7 points
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline in the week immediately following a WORKPLACES improvement greater than 15 points, the reopening-recovery mechanism is rejected.
